name: Goldenes Dachl
kurzbeschreibung: The Goldenes Dachl in Innsbruck's old town is Tyrol's iconic landmark: 2,657 fire-gilded copper shingles, Moriskentänzer reliefs, and a Maximilian museum.
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous Goldenes Dachl on Herzog-Friedrich-Straße in the heart of Innsbruck's historic old town is the unmistakable landmark of the Tyrolean provincial capital and one of Austria's most significant Late Gothic monuments. With its 2,657 fire-gilded copper shingles, the magnificent Late Gothic heraldic oriel balcony has shone over the bustling town square for more than half a millennium. It symbolizes Innsbruck's golden age around 1500, when the city rose to become the political and cultural center of a globe-spanning empire under the Habsburg ruler Kaiser Maximilian I..

History & Architecture

The oriel was constructed between 1497 and 1500 on the front facade of the so-called Neuhof, the former residence of the Tyrolean sovereign rulers. The occasion for the bold construction was the turn of the century as well as Maximilian's marriage to Bianca Maria Sforza of Milan. Construction was directed by the ducal court master builder Nikolaus Türing der Ältere; court painter Jörg Kölderer executed the richly colored frescoes on the oriel wall. The steep oriel roof is covered with exactly 2,657 fire-gilded copper shingles, which sparkle like pure gold in the sunlight to this day. The sandstone balustrade reliefs represent masterpieces of Late Gothic sculpture: they portray Maximilian surrounded by his two wives, court jesters, imperial coats of arms, and the famous Moriskentänzer in bizarre, acrobatic contortions. The oriel served the monarch as a stately imperial box from which he watched knightly tournaments, festive dances, and bustling town markets. Today, the building houses the cutting-edge Museum Goldenes Dachl, which illuminates the life of the emperor and the history of the city with interactive stations, original artifacts, and a dedicated children's trail.

Visit & Getting There

The exterior of the Goldenes Dachl in the pedestrianized old town can be admired free of charge around the clock, all year round. The Museum Goldenes Dachl inside the building is open from May to September daily from 10:00 to 17:00; from October to April Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Mondays). Museum admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €6.00, concessions and seniors €3.50, children and youth under 19 free; family ticket €12.00. Admission is free with the Innsbruck Card. Arrival by public transit: from Innsbruck Central Station, an easy ten-minute stroll leads through the pedestrian area; tram lines (1, 3) and buses stop at Marktplatz or Maria-Theresien-Straße. By car: Inntal Autobahn A12 (exit Innsbruck Ost or West), parking in the Altstadtgarage am Innrain or Markthallengarage.

Tips

The entire pedestrian zone in front of the oriel is smoothly paved and barrier-free accessible. The Museum Goldenes Dachl inside is exemplarily barrier-free: via a lifting platform and modern elevators, wheelchair users and families with strollers enjoy step-free access to all exhibition rooms and directly into the ceremonial oriel. The best photo opportunity of the gilded shingles is in the morning under bright sunlight or from the viewing platform of the opposite Stadtturm.
